- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  Conformance claims are the self-certification blind spot (gh-1834):
  when the final claim includes parity/conformance to a reference or
  specification (any domain), a "verified" item counts only with
  negative and combination checks — refused incompatible options,
  empty/corrupt inputs, boundary values, must-NOT-work cases — alongside
  happy paths; a blanket "everything matches" is not verified (prompt
  step 2.6, conditional: tasks with no conformance claim are
  unchanged).

  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared

  the SEAL (`Session.seal`, gh-1589): after the usage fold + the

  exited (kill + bounded reap on every path, incl. external cancel; loud

  explicit reply rides BOTH parent-visible renders verbatim when in
  budget (`_renderResultBody` — the #1829 envelope when over); the

  recorded; the `reply` ack is truthful (`ReplyRecordOutcome` — a missing

  a false "delivered"; the ack waits out `persistNow`), double reply is
  idempotent (first wins), `task_observe` echoes the deliverable payload

  child's completion is PUBLISHED through the same
  `TaskJobManager.completions` async-result envelope every host consumes
  (`TaskExecutor.resultPublisher` → `publishResumed`): the resumed final
  answer replaces the stored `agent://<id>` output, and a reply acked in
  a killed previous life is carried onto the resume as a resolvable
  artifact (`peekPendingReply` → `DeliverableCapture.persistCarriedReply`
  → `clearPendingReply` — the handle clears only after the artifact is
  durable, so a failed carry leaves the reply resumable)
  — never silence. gh-1948: the executor flushes each
  child's transcript at every turn boundary (the JSONL exists and grows
  mid-run), and `task_observe` resolves a placeholder-handle child
  (`<parentSessionId>/<id>` until the first flush) through
  `resolveChildSessionPath` (`child_session_io.dart` — the sessions-tree
  header scan) wired by the CLI via `SubagentServices.resolveChildSessionPath`,
  healing the handle onto the real path; read failures degrade to a
  structured "no transcript available yet"/"transcript unavailable"
  message, never an uncaught exception. Child IDENTITY for tool calls is
  zone-scoped (`subagent_scope.dart`, gh-970): `runSpawn`/`resumeChild`
  publish the running child's id via `runWithSubagentScope`, and
  `TaskExecutor.currentSubagentId` reads the zone FIRST — the executor's
  in-flight id stack is shared by all concurrent children, so its head is
  "started last", not "executing" (that shift mislabeled every sender
  envelope and recorded replies on sibling handles). Hosts also resolve
  shared tools' self-mailbox semantics through the zone (`activeSubagentId`
  → `schedule_message`'s `senderMailbox`), and the CLI wires
  `SubagentManager.wakeChild` so mail that fires into a finished child's
  inbox (a self-scheduled reminder, sibling mail) resumes it in its own
  session — the child-side analog of the idle inbox wake (the sweep is
  `wakeChildrenWithPendingMail`, status-gated to completed/idle, one wake
  per child per settle, a throwing wake retires the child).

  inbox mail) arriving DURING a tool-call phase cancels the phase's
  zone-scoped yield token — `currentYieldToken()` in `cancel_token.dart`,
  published by `_runToolCallPhase` (`agent_loop.dart`), fed by
  `AgentLoopConfig.steeringNotifications` (in-process queue) and the
  non-draining `hasPendingSteering` probe (external inbox, 2s poll).
  Yield-aware tools (`bash`, blocking `task`) finish the tool call early
  WITHOUT stopping the work — it continues as a background job and the user
  message is delivered at the step boundary. Tools ignoring the token keep
  the classic behavior (message waits for the phase).
- `lib/src/messaging/` — the agent messaging fabric: every agent (main,
  subagents, other Fa instances sharing the root) owns a file inbox behind
  the isolated `MessagingRepository` interface (send/peek/drain/directory —
  future DB/network impls drop in without caller changes).
  `AgentMessage.kind` distinguishes agent chat from `user` input handed
  over by an attached client (the Fa app's attach view; the CLI delivers
  it as `[from app] …`, its own words, not agent chat).

  agent dirs, torn writes skipped. `SubagentManager.messaging` routes

  hidden behind the tool's `all: true` (`.id` markers keep real ids despite

  (the address pinned at schedule time goes stale on session switch/restart
  and would strand the reminder) — EXCEPT self-addressed records naming a
  subagent mailbox of this session (`<prefix>/<childId>`, gh-970): those

  stable; re-addressing stole the child's reminder into main), and the
  tool's `senderMailbox` override (host-wired from `activeSubagentId()`)
  makes a subagent's no-`to` schedule default to the CHILD's mailbox, not
  main's — hosts re-arm on every mailbox change
  (CLI `_syncMailboxPrefix`, app `_setMailboxPrefix`) and sweep due records
  on their inbox ticks; `dispose()` cancels only the timer, the files stay.

  (`from` rewritten alongside `to` in `_deliverDueInner`) — an adopted
  reminder keeps the self shape (from == to) the wake policy needs to
  classify it exempt, so a chain survives a session-id change. Every
  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).

  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.

 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —

 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...                                 first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>                             full commit SHA (the default third-party form)
#   - IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/*@main  owner directive 2026-10-04: awf tracks
#     @main (always-latest, review-gated) — scoped EXACTLY to this repo at
#     exactly main; enforced per-stub by
#     test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart (every awf uses: resolves
#     to exactly 'main', all five stubs in lockstep).
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, master, short SHAs, other repos
# at main) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
# Default (CI) mode: composite actions live under .github/actions/, OUTSIDE
# the workflows dir — root the manifest sweep at the repo root so they
# are covered (a regression here would let an unpinned remote uses: sail
# through AC1). Prune .worktrees: sibling checkouts are not this repo's
# gate surface. Fixture mode (--path) stays rooted at DIR: fixtures are
# self-contained trees.
root="$dir"
if [ "$dir" = ".github/workflows" ] && [ -d "$dir" ]; then
  root="."
fi
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$root" -name .git -prune -o -path './.worktrees' -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2

timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # gh-1778: caches are best-effort — a restore that hangs (degraded
      # cache service stalled both steps ~133 s on the v1.0.621 release
      # run) or fails only means slower setup. Step-level 2-min cap bounds
      # the stall; continue-on-error keeps a dead cache from reding the
      # shard (unlike the gh-1724 evidence uploads, which stay loud).
      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      # gh-2074 rework: the shard's `dart test` is the first hook consumer —
      # on a cold cache + GitHub release-download brownout the hook's bare
      # download 504'd and red'd the leg. Seed the cache with bounded
      # retries + status gating + hash verification first; hook-free
      # invocation (--disable-dart-dev) so the pre-warm cannot die in the
      # very hook it pre-warms for.
      - name: Pre-warm sqlite3 hook assets
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart --disable-dart-dev scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm.dart --package . --targets host

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).

# arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-2074 rework: this leg had NO hooks cache and its boot prewarm
      # below was the first hook consumer — the bare libsqlite3.arm64.linux.so
      # download 504'd (exit 255) in the 2026-11-09 brownout. Restore the
      # shared cache (same key family as the other hosted lanes) and seed it
      # hook-free before the boot prewarm.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: Pre-warm sqlite3 hook assets
        run: dart --disable-dart-dev scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm.dart --package . --targets host
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        env:
          # Issue #1391: same load-stretch as the PTY/CLI shards above —
          # this merge-blocking leg drives the real CLI through the same
          # harness waits and shares the dispatch-wave packing.
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

  coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, test-core]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

name: 'Flutter pub get (enforced lockfile, bounded retry)'
description: >-
  The ONE sanctioned flutter_app dependency-resolution step:
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` with the #726 bounded retry. pub
  has no retry for its git-dependency mirror clones (flutter_js,
  flutter_js_widget_runtime) — one transient "Connection reset by peer" on
  github.com:443 failed the whole leg (#726 on the iOS release leg; gh-1310
  on ci.yml build-macos, where the v1.0.516 lockfile refresh cold-missed
  the flutter-action pub cache and forced fresh clones exactly when a
  release lands). Deterministic pubspec/lockfile skews (gh-1299: a release
  commit that bumps the version without regenerating flutter_app/
  pubspec.lock) fail identically on every attempt — the loop detects the
  "Unable to satisfy" signature and fails fast instead of burning ~30s per
  red leg and blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3). Guarded by
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart: no workflow run-step may resolve
  flutter_app itself.

inputs:
  working-directory:
    description: 'Directory holding the pubspec.yaml to resolve.'
    required: false
    default: flutter_app

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile (bounded retry, #726)
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      env:
        # Git-dep clones must never hang a leg on a credential prompt.
        GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        LOG_FILE="$(mktemp)"
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
          if flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_FILE"; then
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 0

content.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK and the AGP-default CMake so
  Gradle configuration never triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download
  mid-build. gh-1655: one truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download
  ("Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android
  leg — and the aggregate Quality gate with it — because AGP's
  in-configuration auto-install path has NO retry. gh-1757: the same leg
  died the same way on the sibling component — the `:jni` module
  (transitive `jni` package via path_provider_android) wires
  externalNativeBuild.cmake with no version, so AGP auto-installs its
  default cmake;3.22.1 mid-configuration and one corrupt archive
  ("Archive is not a ZIP archive") red'd v1.0.619's build-android leg, the
  aggregate Quality gate, and the Advance vpinned marker job with it. The
  NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's own gradle plugin
  source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves to — no second pin
  to drift), the CMake version is the AGP default cross-checked against
  the AGP pin by the guard test, both installs are skipped when the
  component is already present, and each download is bounded-retried —
  the same hardening the (since-removed) flutter_gemma Android seed
  carried (gh-1468).
  Companion guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK + AGP-default CMake (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1

(3 attempts × timeouts + delays) are finite, but a step-level `timeout-minutes` would keep the

🪶 **NIT: `timeoutPerAttempt` arms two timers — the real per-attempt ceiling is ~2× the named 60 s**

```dart
final stream = await fetch(uri).timeout(timeoutPerAttempt);
final builder = await stream
    .fold<BytesBuilder>(...)
    .timeout(timeoutPerAttempt);   // ← second 60 s timer
```

For the default fetcher the body is fully buffered inside `fetch()`, so only the first timer can
fire and the practical cap matches the documented "60s/attempt". But for an injected fetcher
returning a lazy/slow stream, both timers run back-to-back — worst case ~120 s per attempt, ~8 min
per asset across 3 attempts + delays, vs the documented 60 s. Either fold both stages under one
combined deadline (`.timeout` on a chained future) or note the 2× semantics in the doc comment so
the CI timeout math stays honest.
